A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same robust clustered DPFL research, despite changes to the title and algorithm name. The complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D report original classification, clustering and fairness experiments on MNIST, FMNIST and CIFAR10.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendices E–F report original classification, clustering-confidence, sensitivity and cluster-count estimation results.

M1.justification: The three-stage core is retained as R-DPCFL, but v2 adds confidence-based cluster-count estimation and switching-time selection. Appendix D.6 introduces private accuracy-based cluster selection restricted to 10% of rounds. Algorithm 1 also changes aggregation from dataset-size weights to equal client weights.

E1.justification: The MNIST, FMNIST and CIFAR10 classification settings with covariate or concept shift remain. V2 additionally evaluates recovering an unknown cluster count in Appendix E.3 and Figure 9, whereas v1 required the count as input. Dataset-size sweeps otherwise remain within existing coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds Local and MR-MTL and removes KM-CDPFL from the reported comparisons. The f-CDPFL/IFCA loss-based comparator is retained but substantively adapted for private accuracy-based selection. DPFedAvg and the oracle remain under the names Global and O-DPCFL, including in Appendix F.

E3.justification: The main privacy-budget grid replaces epsilon 2 with 15, and v2 accounts jointly for training and private selection using RDP. Reported train/test sizes change from 50,000/10,000 to 48,000/12,000 for FMNIST and to 40,000/10,000 for CIFAR10 (v1 Table 2; v2 Table 3). V2 removes explicit privacy-cost, worst-client and disparity metrics and adds confidence and cluster-count evaluation protocols.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's batch-size illustrations and privacy/heterogeneity comparisons, v2 adds later-round batch-size sensitivity, local-dataset-size analysis, cluster-count recovery, confidence versus clustering success, and empirical checks supporting Lemma 4.2. These appear in Figures 3, 6, 8, 9, 12 and 14.

E5.justification: V1 Tables 3–10 report averages over three seeds; v2 Figures 4–5 and 10–11 report four runs or seeds. The cluster-count study reports five random data splits in Figure 9. This changes reported replication without introducing a new confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: V1's detailed fairness and majority-client result entries disappear, while v2 reports replacement accuracy/clustering curves and new Local/MR-MTL results. Appendix E.3 newly reports perfect cluster-count recovery on MNIST and FMNIST and 17 correct CIFAR10 cases out of 20. These are added or replaced results under modified settings, not controlled performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: Lemma 4.2 replaces v1's approximately unchanged noise scale with a rho-dependent overlap bound and revised derivation. V2 adds separation/confidence definitions, a worked clustering counterexample, and formal RDP/z-CDP privacy analysis including Theorem G.1. Theorem 4.3 also drops v1's explicitly listed regularity conditions.

C1.justification: V1's central promise of privacy-cost equity across majority and minority clients shifts toward robust sample-level private clustering under structured heterogeneity. V2 adds claims about advantages over local/personalized training and easy parameter selection. Disparate-impact mitigation remains in the conclusion but no longer organizes the abstract and contributions.

C2.justification: V2 develops explanations based on the tradeoff between heterogeneity and noise reduction through federation. It replaces v1's augmentation-based small-data discussion with smaller later-round batches and clustering confidence. The known-cluster-count limitation is replaced by an estimation strategy, while scarce cross-device data becomes an explicit remaining limitation.

D1.justification: Appendices D–E add substantial implementation information: training budgets, validation and hyperparameter grids, private-selection budgets, GMM initialization and covariance settings, and the switching-time formula. TensorFlow Privacy and scikit-learn implementations are identified. Much of this is newly disclosed information rather than evidence that previously unspecified settings changed.

R1.justification: V2 substantially repositions the work against Liu et al.'s cross-silo privacy/personalization research and Luo et al.'s private clustering method. It newly relates the variance analysis to Malekmohammadi et al. (2024), expands privacy-accounting and multitask-learning references, and removes several fairness-focused references, including FOCUS.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, contributions and evaluation narrative, alongside retitling the paper and renaming the algorithm. The appendices are reorganized around notation, background, implementation, parameter selection and consolidated proofs; much fairness-related discussion moves to Appendix J.

P2.justification: V2 adopts two-column main text and substantially redesigns the displays. The threat model is redrawn and moved from v1 Figure 6 to v2 Figure 1, alongside a new process diagram. Detailed result tables and per-cluster bars give way to redesigned accuracy/clustering panels, with additional diagnostic plots and a notation table.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses important omissions in v1: cluster-selection privacy costs (Appendices C.4/D.6) and operation without a known cluster count (Appendix E.3). Substantial implementation details and Local/MR-MTL comparisons strengthen reproducibility and evaluation. Losing direct fairness measurements and retaining inconsistencies between Algorithm 1 and its private-selection implementation are drawbacks, but the gains in methodological completeness and practical support constitute a substantial net improvement.
